LESSON GOALS
•	 To understand simple stories and conversations.
•	 To give and follow simple directions and instructions.
•	 To ask and answer questions about familiar topics 
(personal information, clothes, colours, weather, etc.).
•	 To understand and talk about dates and numbers.
•	 To talk about things you can see in different places 
in the world and things you can buy or do in a shop.
MATERIALS
•	 TR#4 What Do You Do?
•	 TR#12 The Toyshop Song
•	 TR#14 Take a Walk Version 1
•	 TR#20 Time to Go Home
•	 Moods A5 flash cards 
•	 Calendar (P.E.M.1)
•	 Pam&Paul Board Game
•	 Pam&Paul Board Game Reference Sheet
•	 Teacher materials for Act. 2: A3 Supermarket (P.2.2) + 
food cutouts + cloth bag
•	 Teacher materials for Act. 6: Shop cards (P.2.5) + ball
•	 Teacher materials for Act. 1: Characters and Places 
(P.2.1)
•	 Teacher materials for Act. 8: A3 Map (P.2.3)
•	 Red and green stickers (1 of each per child)
•	 Dice and counters (1 per S)
•	 Blu-Tack
BEFORE CLASS
If it’s the last day of the story, check the teacher’s dashboard 
to see if the Ss have completed Mission 2.
LESSON PLAN
1.– WARM-UP ROUTINES (12’)
•	 Hello + register + booklets
•	 Calendar
•	 Moods, version 3, track 4 (optional)
•	 My Pet

2.– STORY QUESTIONS (9’)
During today’s lesson plan there won’t be a storytelling activity. 
Instead, the Ss will work on the story in a more interactive way 
by answering comprehension questions.
We recommend incorporating tools such as a bandana or 
buzzer to make it more fun and dynamic. You could also have 
the Ss compete in teams. 
Here are some suggested questions, but you can expand 
them as necessary: 
•	 On what day did Pam and Paul want to go to the 
toyshop? (Saturday)
•	 What did Pam and Paul want to buy at the toyshop?
(video game)
•	 Why could Grandma and Grandpa not take Pam 
and Paul to the toyshop? (doctor’s appointment)
•	 What did Pam and Paul put on their heads? 
(helmet)
•	 Did Pam and Paul first turn right, turn left or go 
straight ahead? (straight ahead)
•	 Where did Pam and Paul first turn left? 
(petrol station)
•	 What came after the petrol station? (greengrocer’s)
•	 Who had the idea to go through the park? (Pam)

> How to Play
Each S will take a food cutout from a cloth bag and their 
classmates will help them to stick it on the Supermarket sheet 
(P.2.2) by giving them instructions on where to place it. 
> Warm-Up
Quickly review the prepositions using your hands: next to, 
between, behind, in front of and opposite. Then review the names 
of the different cutouts found in the cloth bag by asking, “What 
are these? / What is this?” and get the S to reply using a full 
structure, “They are cherries. / It is a turkey!”. Continue in this 
manner until you have gone over all the food items.
NOTE: if your Ss are familiar with the target language, you 
may skip this step.
> Main Activity
Put all the activity cutouts in a cloth bag. Pair up the Ss (S1 and 
S2). Tell the Ss, “Let’s put the food items in the supermarket!”. 
To do the activity, proceed as follows:
•	 S1: Takes a food cutout. 
•	 S2: “What have you got?”
•	 S1: “I’ve got lettuce.”
•	 S2: “Where does the lettuce go?”
•	 S1: “The lettuce goes ....” and places the cutout on the 
correct spot using Blu-Tack.
> Follow-Up
To follow up, ask Ss where the different items are. For example, 
“Jane, where does the lettuce go?”, to which Jane will have to 
answer, “The lettuce goes next to the cherries.”
4.– ACTIVITY 6: FREEZE! (7’)
P.2.5
> Main Activity
The Ss sit on the floor in a circle. Tell them, “Let’s see if 
you remember what you can buy at each shop!”. Place the 
pile of Shop cards (P.2.5) face down in the middle of the circle 
and get the Ss to begin passing the ball. Tell them that when 
you say “Freeze!”, they must stop. Whenever you feel like it,

shout out “FREEZE!” and the S holding the ball must pick up 
a card from the middle of the circle and answer the question, 
“What can you buy at the…?” as quickly as possible. Once Ss 
are used to the game you can make it more dynamic by not 
asking them the question and letting them come up with the 
sentence themselves. For example:
•	 You can buy jumpers at the clothes shop.
•	 You can buy video games at the toy shop.
•	 You can buy muffins at the bakery.
NOTE: you can also play songs from the story to make it 
more dynamic. You can still say “Freeze!” every time you pause 
the song.
5.– ACTIVITY 4: FOLLOWING DIRECTIONS (5’)
> Warm-Up
Put a red sticker on each Ss’ left hand and a green one on 
their right. Then practise left, right and straight ahead by using 
your hands. Say, “Turn left!” and have everybody turn to the left 
(you should too; having your back turned to your Ss is helpful, 
so everybody is pointing to the same left). Do the same with 
right and straight ahead.
Gradually say each command faster and faster.
> Main Activity
Next, the Ss should form a line. When you say, “Go straight 
ahead”, they must pat the person in front of them on the head. If 
you say, “Turn left” Ss must pat the left shoulder of the person 
in front of them and if you say, “Turn right”, their right shoulder. 
Finally, get them (still in a line) to follow your instructions 
but walking around the class pretending to be on a train.
> Advanced Groups
If your Ss have understood the concepts quickly, you can 
let them take on the teacher role and give commands to their 
classmates.
5.– PAM&PAUL BOARD GAME (16’)
P.E.M.4.1
START
FINISH
P.E.M.4

Play as many rounds of the Pam&Paul Board Game as time 
allows.
SET-UP
1.	 The game can be played individually or in groups (this is 
recommended for big groups). Each player/pair chooses 
a counter and places it on the start square.
2.	 Start the game using one of the strategies in the “Starting 
a game” section in the introduction of the TG. 
3.	 Have them roll the dice and move their counter. Depending 
on the colour of the square (category) the Ss land on, ask 
them to perform the challenge mentioned in the Board 
Game Reference Sheet. 
Special squares:
•	 Square with a plane on it: follow the dotted line and 
go back to the start.
•	 Square with Billy on it: follow Billy’s footprints and do 
the challenge.
•	 Square with a bicycle on it: ride down the road and 
do the challenge.
4.	 If they perform the challenge correctly, they can stay 
on the square. If not, give them a second chance by 
rewording or giving them clues. If they still can’t get it, 
they go back to the square they were in before.
5.	 The game ends when someone reaches the finish line.
7.– TIME TO GO HOME (TR#20) (2’)
Sing the Time to Go Home song and have the students form 
a line before leaving the class. 
BONUS
ACTIVITY 1: MATCHING CHARACTERS
P.2.1
P.2.1
> Warm-Up
Quickly review the actions that each character is doing by 
putting the Place cards (P.2.1) down on the table. Say, “Grandpa

and Grandma are going to the doctor’s, Mum is going to the 
hairdresser’s, and Dad is doing the gardening.”
Show the Ss the X cards and ask, “Why can’t Mum take 
Pam and Paul to the toyshop?”, to which they should reply, 
“Because she is going to the hairdresser’s.” Continue in this 
manner until you have gone over all the pairs.
NOTE: if your Ss are familiar with the target language, you 
may skip this step.
> Main Activity
To introduce the activity, say, “Let’s see if you remember 
what Pam and Paul’s family are doing!”. Put the P.2.1 cards 
in two piles face down: X cards on one side, Place cards on 
the other. The Ss must flip a card from each pile to match the 
character with the correct reason for them to not be able to 
take Pam and Paul to the toyshop.
If they have a match, they should say, “Mum can’t take 
Pam and Paul to the toyshop, because she is going to the 
hairdresser’s. I’ve got a pair!” If they don’t, they should say 
“I’ve got Grandpa and Grandma and doing the gardening; it’s 
not a pair, what a shame!”
> Correct matches and structures
•	 Mum + going to the hairdresser’s: “Mum (she) can’t take 
Pam and Paul to the toyshop because she is going to 
the hairdresser’s.” 
•	 Dad + doing the gardening: “Dad (he) can’t take Pam and 
Paul to the toyshop because he is doing the gardening.” 
•	 Grandma and Grandpa + going to the doctor’s: “Grandma 
and Grandpa (they) can’t take Pam and Paul to the 
toyshop because they are going to the doctor’s.” 
> Follow-Up
Quickly split the group into two teams. Show team A the X 
card and team B the matching place card. Each team should 
say the part of the structure corresponding to their card. For 
example:
•	 Team A: “Grandpa and Grandma can’t take Pam 
and Paul to the toyshop...”
•	 Team B: “...because they are going to the doctor’s.”

ACTIVITY 8: TAKE A WALK (VERSION 1) (TR#14)
P.2.3
> How to Play
This version of this activity is played like the musical chairs 
game.
> Warm-Up
Place the A3 Map (P.2.3) in the middle of the table and do a 
little warm-up by saying “If you find the charity shop, point it 
out to me!” and have all your Ss point to the right place on the 
map. Continue in this manner until you have gone over some 
of the shops that are mentioned in the song.
NOTE: if your Ss are familiar with the target language, you 
may skip this step.
> Main Activity
Introduce the activity by saying, “Let’s take a walk around 
town!”. Leave the map on the table and play the song Take a 
Walk Version 1 (TR#14). The Ss should walk around the table 
singing the song but, when you pause the track after each 
shop, the first S to point to the correct shop on the map should 
sit down so that the rest of their classmates can have a go at 
this activity as well.
> Follow-Up
If time allows, ask each S, “What can you buy at the...?” 
and the Ss individually, each saying a different item, should 
say, “You can buy ... at the...”. Challenge them to come up with 
items they haven’t learned in class.
